timing: Untimed source correspondence only. Derive cuts from actual approved speech and genuine transcript anchors. No estimated timings.

spans.text: This lesson maintains an existing IC command board in a fictional warehouse exercise. The screens come from the same saved exercise across browser sessions. Begin in Call Details and verify the Warehouse alarm name and training location.
spans.purpose: Actual loaded call identity, location and existing active-command entry.

spans.text: Active Command and Open Command Board identify the available route into this incident. Choose Open Command Board.
spans.purpose: Readable existing-board entry; no start, reopen or template-selection claim.

spans.text: Check the incident name again on Command Board, along with Wallace Boden as commander. Before practicing, make this identity check a habit; similar lane names can appear on different incidents.
spans.purpose: Actual board identity and commander, with the original command left active.

spans.text: Command Structure shows Search Division and Staging. Squad 3 is already in Search Division; Staging has no assigned resource. Rotate and Requirements are review cues on the saved assignment. They do not move the unit automatically.
spans.purpose: Existing saved lane allocation and visible advisory badges; no lane edit or move shown.

spans.text: Scroll to Resources. All is selected, with Unassigned and Assigned available beside it. The pool contains Squad 3, Engine 51 and the fictional Exercise Gate Marshal.
spans.purpose: Actual three-entry pool and filter controls, without implying a filter-result demonstration.

spans.text: Engine 51 names Christopher Herrmann in its Officer or Team Lead position while the unit remains unassigned to a lane. Crew membership and command allocation describe different things. For practice, explain that difference before proposing a move.
spans.purpose: Actual occupied riding position and UNASSIGNED command-lane badge; no crew or resource mutation claimed.

spans.text: In Tactical Objectives, choose Add. The empty section gives us a clear starting point.
spans.purpose: Readable empty objectives section and its actual Add control, before the benchmark existed.

spans.text: In Add Objective, select Benchmark under Type and enter the training primary-search objective. Choose Add to save it. A specific objective name gives the next operator something concrete to review.
spans.purpose: Prepared Benchmark form, entered training name and Add; subsequent actual saved objective supplies the result.

spans.text: Open the objective and use Progress to set fifty percent. The returned details show fifty percent selected. Outcome, Close-out note and Complete Objective describe a separate close-out decision. This exercise leaves the objective incomplete. Practice updating progress without treating an estimate as a completed search.
spans.purpose: Actual saved 50% details and unsubmitted completion controls. No outcome or completion was saved.

spans.text: In the Needs section, use Add to open Add Need. Choose Medical under Category. Enter the training rehab need, set Qty to two, and use Details to explain the gap: two fictional rehab positions at staging, for internal tracking.
spans.purpose: Complete visible foreground Add Need form; background labels are not used as evidence.

spans.text: Choose Add after checking the name and quantity. This example records a quantified need; it does not request a provider or demonstrate anyone arriving.
spans.purpose: Actual Add control, prepared quantity and explicit fictional internal scope.

spans.text: Open the saved need. Its heading still shows an open medical need with zero of two filled. For practice, describe what remains outstanding before entering a fill.
spans.purpose: Actual OPEN / MEDICAL • 0/2 saved state; Fill contains an unsaved one, handled in the next chapter.

spans.text: In the need details, set Fill to one of two. Enter an explicit training explanation in Note or Reason, then choose Save Fill. The number is a tracking entry; it is not evidence of a person reaching staging.
spans.purpose: Visible prepared Fill 1, reason and Save Fill; no external request or arrival claim.

spans.text: Reopen the need. Partial Fill and one of two now describe the saved result. History attributes the change to Wallace Boden and retains the training reason.
spans.purpose: Actual reopened 1/2 Partial Fill and its attributed saved audit entry.

spans.text: The board also shows the need at one of two beside the objective at fifty percent. Leave the remaining gap visible. For practice, explain why a partial fill should remain distinguishable from completing or closing the need.
spans.purpose: Returned board with both saved working states; neither need closure nor objective completion is shown.

spans.text: Scroll to Notes and choose Add Note. Give the next operator a concrete location and scope. Our note keeps staging at the fictional west gate and explicitly says there is no operational deployment.
spans.purpose: Actual empty Notes section and Add Note entry, followed by the prepared foreground form.

spans.text: Under Visibility, select Internal. The helper says the note is visible to command staff only and that the log records who added it, rather than its text. Public is a different choice. Check the intended audience, then choose Save.
spans.purpose: Actual Internal selection, Public alternative, exact helper and Save control.

spans.text: After reopening the board, the note retains its Internal badge and body. Below it, ICS Role Assignments names Matthew Casey as Safety Officer. That existing command role is separate from a unit riding position or lane assignment. Practice checking the note audience before using a shared command device.
spans.purpose: Actual retained note and existing role after full reload; no role-assignment, message or file-upload operation claimed.

spans.text: Timers and PAR shows the existing Training PAR reminder as overdue, with Acknowledge available. Its elapsed time reflects the saved exercise across sessions. This recording does not acknowledge or restart it. A reminder needs a deliberate operational response; its badge alone says nothing about a crew member's condition.
spans.purpose: Actual persisted overdue reminder and untouched Acknowledge control.

spans.text: Now read Accountability. The call says check-in timers are active, but no timers are configured. Refresh is visible, but this empty configuration cannot demonstrate a successful check-in or a PAR result.
spans.purpose: Actual empty Accountability section and exact no-configuration message.

spans.text: For practice, explain which information is missing before asking a crew to rely on this display.
spans.purpose: Keep the configuration limitation on screen while discussing its operational consequence.

spans.text: On Incident Map, check the actual Chicago street map and Squad 3 marker with its Search Division label. These are fictional training positions, not a demonstration of device GPS.
spans.purpose: Actual v3 camera rendering on genuine Chicago cartography and named training assignment.

spans.text: Pan to frame the surrounding streets, then choose Save View. Here the manual pan moves the marker to the right of center.
spans.purpose: Actual manually panned framing and Save View, without invented coordinates or a drawn route.

spans.text: Reopening the incident map retains that framing.
spans.purpose: Actual return through the board and reopened incident map; the entry button itself was not captured.

spans.text: A full browser reload retains it too. Pan and Save View were verified in this web recording. Line, Area and Text are visible, but annotation placement was not verified. Native touch, location and offline behavior need separate device checks. Practice saving a useful view and checking the returned map.
spans.purpose: Actual full-reload retained framing and visible annotation controls; no web annotation, native or offline outcome claimed.

spans.text: Return to the board and scroll to Incident Log. Read the timestamped objective addition, progress update and need-fill entry. They connect the working cards to attributed actions.
spans.purpose: Actual persisted log contains objective add/progress and need add/fill entries.

spans.text: The internal note has a non-public log marker with its author; its body stays out of this log entry. The map-created entry is also present after Save View.
spans.purpose: Actual non-public-note attribution without its body and actual map entry after save/reload.

spans.text: For handover practice, compare this history with the saved cards, identify the remaining one-of-two gap, and state that the objective is still incomplete. Leave this training command active. This lesson verifies recorded application state; it does not establish a field deployment, delivered notification or completed accountability check.
spans.purpose: Read-only handover review; no Transfer, End Command, call closure, provider delivery or physical outcome claimed.
